<reason>A very tight debate that narrowed cleanly to the meaning of "stronger" and whether "only" adds anything. PRO argued memorably (the nurse, "the condition protects the freedom," "vote for the weld") and made a clever move redefining "stronger" as relative to the prior license's obligations, while pressing a convergence narrative. But CON held one consistent distinction from opening to close—adequacy for the proposed hours versus mandatory change—and PRO's own A2 concession ("then nothing") plus its closing admission that attaching an already-binding plan may close no gap left the motion's "only" defended as a zero-cost formality rather than added protection. CON answered both pressure questions directly with clean A1/A2, neutralized the 400-capacity transit example (assessment covers all three risks regardless of trigger), and dissolved the alleged transit contradiction (necessary vs. unnecessary delay). PRO's convergence story also somewhat overstated CON's movement, since CON's opening already endorsed pre-approval conditions where gaps exist. Two clipped PRO turns cost it the close of its key arcs. Narrow but real edge to CON for making the decisive question easier to resolve.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's B4.5–B4.8 answering PRO's stranded-crowd hypothetical and "stronger" redefinition: showing that comprehensive assessment already asks about the last train, that "risk-specific" governs remedies not which risks are assessed, and that duplicating already-binding obligations on a license "closes no gap"—which forced PRO's closing to concede "perhaps" and fall back on a zero-cost signature.</best_rebuttal>
